messages:
maya: quick share from this morning's geo sweep — ran gpt-open-7b q4_0 on A100 vs H100 across us-central1 and eu-west1. highlights: prefill variance is bigger than i expected (EU prefill ~18% slower on A100), decode throughput favored H100 by ~30% for long decodes. :thinking_face:
chris: nice, numbers?
devin: can you paste the exact cmd you used? i'll re-run on our dedicated pool.
maya: command I used: ```rbench --model gpt-open-7b --quant q4_0 --gpu {a100,h100} --region {us-central1,eu-west1} --batch 1 --prompt-tokens 512 --decode-tokens 1024 --iters 120```
maya: key micro-results (median over runs):
- us-central1 A100: prefill 72ms, decode (per token) 1.9ms, tokens/sec 520, $/1M tokens = $18.4
- us-central1 H100: prefill 64ms, decode (per token) 1.4ms, tokens/sec 680, $/1M tokens = $20.1
- eu-west1 A100: prefill 86ms, decode (per token) 2.1ms, tokens/sec 470, $/1M tokens = $19.2
- eu-west1 H100: prefill 70ms, decode (per token) 1.6ms, tokens/sec 620, $/1M tokens = $21.0
chris: interesting — H100 is faster but cost per 1M tokens is higher in our pricing fabric, so tradeoff depends on latency SLOs. :money_with_wings:
samir: did you try kernel fallbacks / mixed kernels? that can change decode perf for q4_0.
maya: yes, for H100 we saw kernel autotune pick fused attention for decode which improves throughput. for A100 it sometimes fell back to the generic kernel on EU hosts (driver mismatch on a subset), hence higher prefill. added logs: ```ATTN_KERNEL=generic fallback_count=7```
devin: bump infra-bot to repro the driver mismatch on eu-west1 A100 fleet?
infra-bot: ticket created #INF-3145 — scheduling node-level driver audit in eu-west1. assigned to @samir. ETA 48h.
samir: thanks. if driver fix reduces fallbacks we might close the gap on prefill. also worth testing q8_0 quant to see $/1M delta.
maya: good call — quick q8_0 sweep shows tokens/sec up ~8% on both SKUs and cost drops ~$2/M on the A100 side. will post a short CSV later.
chris: for capacity planning: under our 99th pct SLO (prefill+first 64 tokens <= 200ms) H100 in eu meets it, A100 in eu fails on about 12% of requests today. that's enough to trigger fallback routing to us which increases cross-zone egress.
maya: routing note: we saw cross-zone fallbacks add ~0.7c per 1k requests egress. small but accumulative.
devin: can you attach the raw traces? i'll run the latency tail analyzer.
maya: attaching gist in thread: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-1729944444 (contains full csv + sample traces).
samir: TL;DR — H100 wins latency and throughput, A100 wins on raw $/token at current pricing in us, but driver/kernel health in eu makes A100 less reliable. recommend: short term — route critical low-latency traffic to H100 in eu, long-term — driver remediation + q8 sweep to improve A100 economics.
maya: agreed. I'll open a rollout plan for canary routing + cost delta dashboard. :white_check_mark:
